notes.title: The best platform games on PC
notes.content:
The biggest names in platforming used to live only on console, but it’s on PC now that the genre is thriving. Indies have taken the simple ingredients and spun them off in umpteen directions (but still normally from left to right). Below you’ll find a collection of the very best platform games on PC – including puzzle platformers, physics platformers, platformers with roguelike elements, and platformers about absolutely nothing but pixel-perfect jumping.

notes.title: Bugfix update 11/5/2018
notes.content:
Thanks to everybody who joined up on the beta branch to help us fix up some bugs. Please see our changelist below. 

[list][*]Bug-fix "Removed ninja arm tattoos in level 1-2_end and level 1-2_mid_B cutscenes for consistency"
[*]Bug-fix "Fix for 'Reset to Defaults' in the settings screen reverting to Borderless at 30%. Now it reverts to 100%"
[*]Bug-fix "Now saving games asynchronously so there should be fewer framerate hitches during gameplay"
[*]Bug-fix "Mouse cursor is now hidden when a gamepad is used"
[*]Bugfix: "Changed the mouse cursor to the previous custom mouse cursor"
[*]Addition: Borderless Fullscreen scaling factor now also shows the render target size.
[*]Bug-fix: "Removed sword from Path of Silence and Path of Wisdom images."
[*]Bug-fix: "Fix for retina screens not displaying the correct borderless fullscreen render target size"
[*]Addition: "Now able to toggle 'Preload Levels' option in settings screen, intended for people who are experiencing slow level streaming. It will use 600Mb more memory and increase the initial loading time, but any slow streaming issues during gameplay should be resolved."
[*]Fixed an issue with interference from motion sensors when using PS4 controllers under Linux.
[*]Fixed several rendering issues with AMD cards under Linux.
[*]Fixed some art inconsistencies
[*]Bug-fix: "Fixed crash on shutdown on Linux."
[*]Bug-fix: "Now hiding mouse on startup."
[*]Bug-fix: "Fixed a bug where the game would report a failed save when using a flag mid-level"
[*]Bug-fix: "Dosan expansion label was not showing up for some languages."
[*]Bug-fix: "Light overlay texture fixed which was causing light beams to be darker than they should be. Also fixes lightning in Hessian Castle levels."
[*]Bug-fix: "Fix for commentary strings being cut off"[/list]

notes.title: Mark Of The Ninja: Remastered leaps out of the shadows
notes.content:
I hardly ever revisit singleplayer games, so the fact that I’ve snuck all the way through Mark Of The Ninja two and a half times should tell you something. One and a half of those times actually involved just as much stabbing and shuriken tossing as sneaking, but shh.

I say this because Mark Of The Ninja: Remastered has slunk out of the shadows, boasting prettier visuals, snazzier sound, and the extra items and level from the Special Edition DLC. If this one passed you by, I’d implore you to snap it up. It’s free if you already own the DLC, and discounted to 4 for owners of the non-fancy version.

notes.title: Mark Of The Ninja: Remastered will be a cheap or free upgrade for original owners
notes.content:
Klei Entertainment have announced that Mark Of The Ninja: Remastered, the revamped rerelease of their rad stealth-o-murder-a-platformer from 2012, will launch on October 9th. It’ll boast high-resolution art and improved sound but still be the same fine game at heart, and accordingly won’t be expensive for folks who got Mark Of The Ninja on Steam the first time around. Klei have said that those who got its Special Edition DLC back in the day, which cost 4/$5, will get Remastered for free. If not, hey, original players can just pay an extra 4/$5 now to get Remastered.
